solution:
Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ \frac{5}{3} \\ \frac{4}{3} \end{bmatrix}\).
By \(R_3 \to R_3 - R_1\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ \frac{5}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3} \end{bmatrix}\).
By \(R_3 \to R_3 + R_2\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ \frac{5}{3} \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence the equations are
\(x + y = 1,\quad y + z = \frac{5}{3},\quad 2z = 2\).
From the third, \(z = 1\); then \(y = \dfrac{5}{3} - z = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(x = 1 - y = \frac{1}{3}\).
Therefore \(x = \frac{1}{3},\ y = \frac{2}{3},\ z = 1\).

solution:
Matrix form \(AX = B\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & -4 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 8 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\).
By \(R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & -4 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\).
By \(R_2 \to R_2 - 2R_1,\ R_3 \to R_3 - 3R_1\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & -5 & -13 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ -15 \\ -23 \end{bmatrix}\).
By \(R_3 \to R_3 - R_2\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & -8 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ -15 \\ -8 \end{bmatrix}\).
Hence the equations are
\(x + 2y + 3z = 8,\quad -5y - 5z = -15,\quad -8z = -8\).
From the third, \(z = 1\); then \(-5y - 5(1) = -15 \Rightarrow y = 2\), and \(x + 2(2) + 3(1) = 8 \Rightarrow x = 1\).
Therefore \(x = 1,\ y = 2,\ z = 1\).

solution:
Let \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 1(4 - 4) - 2(-4 - 2) + 3(-2 - 1) = 0 + 12 - 9 = 3 \neq 0\), so \(A^{-1}\) exists.

**Adjoint method.** Cofactors:
\(A_{11} = +(4 - 4) = 0,\ A_{12} = -(-4 - 2) = 6,\ A_{13} = +(-2 - 1) = -3\)
\(A_{21} = -(8 - 6) = -2,\ A_{22} = +(4 - 3) = 1,\ A_{23} = -(2 - 2) = 0\)
\(A_{31} = +(4 - 3) = 1,\ A_{32} = -(2 + 3) = -5,\ A_{33} = +(1 + 2) = 3\)
\(\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & 1 & -5 \\ -3 & 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\,\text{adj}(A) = \dfrac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & 1 & -5 \\ -3 & 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\).

**Elementary transformations.** Write \(A = IA\) and apply row transformations until the left side is \(I\):
By \(R_2 \to R_2 + R_1,\ R_3 \to R_3 - R_1\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}A\)
By \(R_2 \to \frac{1}{3}R_2\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}A\)
By \(R_1 \to R_1 - 2R_2\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3} & 0 \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}A\)
By \(R_1 \to R_1 + \frac{1}{3}R_3,\ R_2 \to R_2 - \frac{5}{3}R_3\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 2 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{5}{3} \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}A\)
Hence \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & 1 & -5 \\ -3 & 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\).

Both methods give the same inverse.

solution:
Let \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 1(2 - 6) - 0(0 - 3) + 1(0 - 2) = -4 + 0 - 2 = -6 \neq 0\), so \(A^{-1}\) exists.
Write \(A = AI\) and apply column transformations until the left side is \(I\):
By \(C_3 \to C_3 - C_1\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = A\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)
By \(C_2 \to \frac{1}{2}C_2\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = A\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)
By \(C_3 \to C_3 - 3C_2\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -3 \end{bmatrix} = A\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & -\frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)
By \(C_3 \to -\frac{1}{3}C_3\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = A\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{1}{3} \end{bmatrix}\)
By \(C_1 \to C_1 - C_3,\ C_2 \to C_2 - C_3\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = A\begin{bmatrix} \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \end{bmatrix}\)
Hence \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix} 4 & -2 & 2 \\ -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\).

solution:
Let \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 4 & 7 \end{bmatrix}\).
\(|A| = 1(7 - 20) - 2(7 - 10) + 3(4 - 2) = -13 + 6 + 6 = -1 \neq 0\), so \(A^{-1}\) exists.
Write \(A = IA\) and apply row transformations until the left side is \(I\):
By \(R_2 \to R_2 - R_1,\ R_3 \to R_3 - 2R_1\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}A\)
By \(R_2 \to -R_2\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}A\)
By \(R_1 \to R_1 - 2R_2\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}A\)
By \(R_1 \to R_1 - 7R_3,\ R_2 \to R_2 + 2R_3\): \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 13 & 2 & -7 \\ -3 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}A\)
Hence \(A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 13 & 2 & -7 \\ -3 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).
